author: NorthEast News Desk
body: The Rhode Island Department of Health issued a repeat boil-water advisory for Prudence Island on Monday while the Prudence Island Water District addresses what officials described as significant deficiencies, Coastal ABC reported. Residents were asked to boil water before drinking, cooking or brushing their teeth.

The advisory follows a 2018 routine sample that tested positive for E. coli. The district reported that 203 subsequent tests found no E. coli, but state officials required additional treatment and monitoring. New facilities for chlorine and iron-and-manganese pretreatment began operating Aug. 4.

Health officials said chlorine levels will be monitored over the next several months as the system operates under the new requirements. The district is expected to continue issuing notices every three months. Residents should follow the current advisory until health officials and the water district announce that it has been lifted.
The advisory is a precaution tied to system compliance and monitoring; it does not mean the 2018 result was a new positive test.
dek: Rhode Island health officials are again asking Prudence Island residents to boil water while the local district addresses treatment and monitoring requirements.
headline: Repeat boil-water advisory issued for Prudence Island
